title: Delete dead Program fields: hideFromDashboard + dayOfWeek
description: Session-137 audit confirmed two Program columns are dead: hideFromDashboard (defined, in the editor form + API CRUD, but NO surface reads it — removeFromProgramList is what actually controls the dashboard Today card) and dayOfWeek (vestigial — code uses recurrenceDays everywhere; schema comment claims it 'drives Today badge + listing day group' but nothing reads it). Remove both: schema.prisma, an ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS in migrate.mjs, and the editor/API references to hideFromDashboard. Deferred from session 137 to keep the offering-kind slice focused and the revert story clean. Verify no reads with a grep before dropping.
notes: Pure hygiene; the fields are inert. Bundle with the removeFromProgramList rename below if doing a Program-schema cleanup pass.

title: Rename Program.removeFromProgramList (it actually controls the dashboard Today card)
description: The field name is misleading: removeFromProgramList does NOT control the public Programs listing (that's hideFromProgramPageList). It gates the dashboard Today card inclusion, with dashboardShowAt as the override. Rename to something honest (e.g. hideFromTodayCard / removeFromTodayCard) across schema, the dashboard query, the ProgramEditor Visibility tab, and the programs-pg API. Load-bearing rename — do it deliberately with a migration that renames the column (or add-new + backfill + drop-old). Deferred from session 137 (churn without functional payoff in that slice).
notes: Documented in the schema comment meanwhile. The session-137 audit flagged the misnomer.

title: Kind picker in the ProgramEditor category-create flow
description: Session 137 put offering KIND on ProgramCategory and added a per-row Kind dropdown to the standalone category manager (/tools/programs/categories). But the OTHER place categories are created — the ProgramEditor's Categories tab inline 'add category' — still creates a category with kind=null (the POST /api/programs-pg/categories accepts kind, it's just not wired into that UI). Null kind falls back safely (treated by registration), but a coordinator who creates a category there has to remember to go set its Kind on the manager page. Add a Kind <select> to the ProgramEditor inline category-create so kind is set at creation. Small.
notes: Deliberate scope cut in session 137 to stay out of the 2000-line ProgramEditor. lib/programKind.ts::PROGRAM_KINDS is the option source.

title: "Community this week" dashboard surface for open offerings
description: From the session-137 design conversation. 'Coming up for you' is personal (registration-driven) and correctly excludes open drop-ins/community groups a member hasn't registered for. But Jesse may want open community life (Recovery Dharma, the silent sits, open community groups) to feel PRESENT on the dashboard without being personal. That's a distinct surface — 'your community this week' / community rhythm — drawn from openly-droppable kinds, shown to everyone, separate from the personal 'Coming up for you'. Today/This-Week already carry this material; this would give it more presence on the home page. Design + build when Jesse wants it.
notes: Keeps 'Coming up for you' meaning *you* while making community offerings visible. Pairs with 2026-06-04-005.

title: "Follow / add to my schedule" signal for open offerings
description: From the session-137 design conversation. An OPEN offering (a drop-in, an open community group with no registration) can't appear in a member's personal 'Coming up for you' today because there's no per-person signal that it's theirs — only registration provides that. If we want members to pull a favorite open drop-in or open community group into their own upcoming list without forcing registration, add a lightweight 'follow / add to my schedule' affordance (a per-member follow record) that 'Coming up for you' also reads. Lovely and on-brand (helping someone hold their practice); a real new capability, so deferred until there's pull for it. Note: registered offerings already flow into 'Coming up' — this is only for the open ones.
notes: The alternative for a community group that should be a commitment is simply to turn on its registration. This follow signal is for genuinely open offerings.

title: Optional: support@ heads-up when a paid registration is abandoned
description: Session 136 added a support@ notification for every COMPLETED registration (fires from the sendRegistrationConfirmation choke point; never for an abandoned hold). LoriLee noticed there's no notification when someone STARTS a paid (required-dana) registration and abandons checkout. We left it out on purpose — an unfinished checkout isn't a registration, and the held PENDING_PAYMENT row auto-expires. But a quiet 'someone began but didn't finish paying' heads-up could let support reach out ('did you hit trouble paying?'). If wanted: fire it from handleRegistrationDanaExpired in app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts (the expired handler that deletes the held row) and/or the cron's hold-deletion path — to a new editable template (Email Template Gate), with the registrant's name/email/program. Weigh against noise/privacy; only build if LoriLee confirms it's useful.
notes: Offered to LoriLee in her session-136 reply; awaiting her call. Don't build by default — it's a 'maybe noise' feature.

title: Multi-day program time label: 'Begins 4 PM CT' vs 'Begins 4:00 PM CT'
description: Session 136 fixed multi-day program labels — a retreat spanning Sep 10–13 now reads 'September 10–13, 2026 · Begins 4 PM CT' instead of the misleading single-day 'September 10, 2026 · 4–12 PM CT'. The time renders 'Begins 4 PM CT' (no ':00') because computeTimeText's fmt() drops :00 minutes everywhere for consistency. If Jesse/LoriLee prefer the begins-time to always show minutes ('Begins 4:00 PM CT'), it's a one-line change in the multi-day branch of computeTimeText — but it must be applied in all THREE mirrored copies (lib/programUtils.ts, components/registrar/ProgramEditor.tsx, prisma/migrate.mjs inlined mirror), and the recache_program_date_time_text migration will repropagate on next deploy. Trivial; only do it if the shorter form reads as too terse in practice.
notes: Cosmetic. The date-range half ('September 10–13, 2026') is the substance and is unaffected.

title: Session room: latency/sync measurement pass
description: Items 2 + 7 from Jesse's session-room list: an occasional slight delay (mouth movement to video) and an intermittent audio/video sync problem. Deliberately NOT code-fixed yet (measure before changing architecture). Needs a real 2-3 person live session: (1) separate overall glass-to-glass lag (normal WebRTC, ~150-250ms, likely not a bug) from lip-sync desync; (2) A/B Krisp by toggling Bell mode (NC off) to see if audio tightens; (3) read chrome://webrtc-internals (or a temporary on-screen stats overlay) for jitter buffer / RTT / packet loss; (4) check CPU (software H.264 encode on older devices). Only then consider codec/bitrate/Krisp changes. See RIM_SessionRoom.md.

title: Session room: pin a participant from mobile/touch
description: The local Pin affordance (session 133) is a hover-reveal button on the tile, so touch devices can't initiate a pin (they can unpin via the always-visible banner). Parity with the Mute button's hover-only limitation. To close the gap for iPad/phone users who want to pin the teacher, add a Pin action to the Participants panel rows (alongside the Message and Mute actions). Small slice.

title: Session room: suppress share-focus for the sharer
description: When someone shares their whole screen, their own focus tile can render blank (the browser captures the screen recursively for the person sharing). Everyone else sees the content fine. Zoom minimizes the self-view. Optional polish: for the sharer specifically, don't auto-focus their own screen-share track (keep them in gallery/speaker, or show a small 'You are sharing' card). Revisit if it bugs hosts in practice.

title: Nudge guests to enter a full name on the session join screen
description: Members now show first + last name in the session room (session 133). Guests on open-access programs type their own free-form name on the /session/[slug]?key= entry screen, so they may enter only a first name or a nickname. Consider a gentle prompt/placeholder encouraging 'First and last name' on that screen, consistent with the community-not-anonymous principle. Low priority; guests are a minority of the room.

title: Remove redundant session checks from /account/(authenticated)/ pages
description: After session 132's route-group layout at app/account/(authenticated)/layout.tsx enforces session + agreedToTerms + archivedAt for the entire authenticated member area, the individual per-page checks like `if (!session) redirect('/login')` inside dashboard/page.tsx and the other (authenticated)/ pages are redundant. The layout runs before the page renders, so by the time any page body executes the user is already authenticated. Leaving them in place is harmless but clutters the code and creates a false sense of where the auth gate lives. Sweep all pages under app/account/(authenticated)/ and remove the now-redundant `if (!session) redirect('/login')` blocks. Pages still need to call auth() to get the session object for their own use (the user's id, roles, etc.) — that part stays. Just drop the redirect-if-null defensive check. Low priority, mechanical cleanup. Could be paired with adding a small `requireSession()` helper if pages want a typed non-null session — but that's optional.

title: Banyan tree image on /join page
description: The Webflow Community Membership page has a banyan-tree image on the right side of the hero — part of the warmth and intentionality of the threshold experience. Not ported to /join in the session-132 slice because the asset wasn't in the repo. When ready: drop the image into public/images/ or Vercel Blob, wire it into app/join/page.tsx as a left/right grid (hero + intro on left, image on right) at desktop, stack on mobile. ~10-line CSS change to add .jn-hero--with-image and adjust .jn-container max-width. Source asset on the live Webflow site at https://www.rootedinmindfulness.org/community-membership — the banyan-tree photo.

title: Add 'Become a Member' link to footer
description: The /join page is currently linked from the Nav (signed-out Member Area dropdown) and from the community-programs hero CTA and the diversity page. A quiet, always-on entry from the footer would let visitors find it from anywhere on the site without expanding a nav dropdown. Add to components/Footer.tsx as a low-emphasis text link in the appropriate column. Probably worth pairing with a footer-design pass since the footer hasn't been formally designed yet.

title: Silent Meditation Hub — peer-led self-claim for Good Morning / Good Evening sits
description: New Hub (working name: silent-sit-team or similar) for the peer-led silent meditation offerings — currently Good Morning Silent Meditation and Good Evening Silent Meditation, with room to grow to Recovery Dharma and any future peer-led offering. Members of the hub can self-claim individual sessions or commit to a standing rotation, mirroring how the Host Team works. The infrastructure mostly already exists and can be reused as-is: HubMember (active members with hostingCapability), HostAssignment (per-session assignment), the self-claim flow at /api/host/assignments POST, the Standing Host Assignments system for recurring patterns, and Step-In to take over a session mid-flight. The new pieces are the Hub record itself (created via /admin/hubs), a coordinator decision about which programs the hub is allowed to claim, and possibly a tweak to the schedule tool (/tools/schedule) so it can also display open silent-sit sessions alongside the host team's. Closely related to backlog 2026-05-25-002 (per-program teacherLabel): together those two items make peer-led offerings first-class in the system — the hub solves 'who's allowed to lead' and teacherLabel solves 'what do we call them when they do.' Build order suggestion: teacherLabel first (small, lights up better audio profile + correct pill name as soon as ProgramTeacher rows exist), then this hub (larger structural piece).
notes: Closed 2026-05-22 (session 128 cumulative). Slice 1 (architecture, commit 500fa64): schema (Program.hostingHubSlug + Hub.assignmentGrantsTeacher + Hub.teacherLabel), helper lib/programHub.ts, resolveSessionRole broadening, LiveKit + host operation route updates, ProgramEditor 'Hosting & Access' tab with field moves, schedule filter, slug validation. Slice 2 (operational): peer-led-silent-meditation hub created via /admin/hubs with assignmentGrantsTeacher: true + teacherLabel: 'Facilitator'; Good Morning + Good Evening Silent Meditation transferred via the Hosting & Access tab; Jesse added as coordinator via new /api/admin/hubs/[slug]/add-me-as-coordinator endpoint that closes the catch-22 from removing ADMIN's hub-content bypass; manual chapter seeded. Slice 2.5 (hub-isolation hardening, commits fdb441d/86ce52e/e446213/a80dc17/03f8537): every outbound email URL hub-scoped via new hubScopedUrl/hubHomeUrl helpers; welcome-email reliability fix via after(); CTA button helper; three new engineering reference docs (RIM_Hub_Engineering, RIM_Email_Engineering, RIM_Scheduler); CLAUDE.md closing ritual gets self-perpetuating per-tool-doc step 4d. Slice 2.6 (standing-rotation generalization, commits 51d1207/d5ad0fc/89051f3): all 6 standing-assignment routes hub-routed by program via getProgramHubSlug; new lib/hubAuth.ts::isHubCoordinator helper; standing-assignment emails accept hubSlug; Rotations tab visibility gated by hub-aware isManager (was global isHostManager only — hid the tab from non-HOST_MANAGER hub coordinators). The original design question from this entry — 'should every Session Host get bell-friendly audio regardless of ProgramTeacher status' — was resolved during the Slice 1 design conversation by the hub-grants-teacher mechanism. Peer-led hubs get teacher capability via hub assignment; the host-team hub keeps assignmentGrantsTeacher: false so its hosts still need a ProgramTeacher row to be a Teacher. Architecture is fully operational + isolated end-to-end; pending only Jesse's live verification of Nancy's end-to-end flow.

title: Per-program teacherLabel dropdown — Teacher / Guide / Facilitator / Instructor
description: Add a nullable Program.teacherLabel String field (default null = display 'Teacher') and a dropdown in the Program editor next to the teacher search letting the coordinator choose what the role pill says for that program. Seeded options: Teacher (default), Guide, Facilitator, Instructor, with room for a custom value. Thread the value through the LiveKit token route's seedMeta (alongside the existing `teacher: true` boolean) so participant metadata carries the label string, and update the pill renderer in RIMParticipantTile + ParticipantsPanel + RIMConference's client-side metadata seeder to display `meta.teacherLabel ?? 'Teacher'` when meta.teacher is true. The mechanism stays exactly the same — a ProgramTeacher row still drives the bell-friendly audio profile and still puts the pill on the tile — only the display string varies per program. This is what makes peer-led silent sits (Guide), Recovery Dharma (Facilitator), and Qigong (Instructor?) all fit the same model without overloading 'Teacher.' Implementation surface: one new field in prisma/schema.prisma, one migration to add the column, one dropdown in components/registrar/ProgramEditor.tsx, one prop addition to the data path (token route → page → VideoRoom → RIMConference → metadata → pill), one comment update on ParticipantMetadata. Maybe an hour's focused work end-to-end.
notes: Closed 2026-05-26 (session 127). Shipped per spec with two reviewer-caught refinements: sanitizer reordered (strip → trim → slice rather than slice → strip) so a long string with disallowed characters doesn't survive the slice, and regex widened from `/[^A-Za-z\s\-]/g` to `/[^\p{L}\p{M}\d\s'\-]/gu` so apostrophes, digits, accented letters, and non-Latin scripts pass (Teacher's Aide, Co-Leader 1, rōshi, etc.). Step-in route also returns teacherLabel for parity with the token route. Custom… revealed input is capped at 20 chars. Commit fbbf955.

title: Add noindex headers to lesson + enrolled-course pages
description: Belt-and-suspenders pass to keep member-only content out of search engines, even though the auth gate already prevents content delivery. Add `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">` (via Next.js `metadata.robots`) to `/lessons/[slug]/page.tsx` and to the enrolled-state branch of `/course/[slug]/page.tsx`. The pre-enrollment landing on `/course/[slug]` stays indexable — it's the public marketing surface (per RIM_Offering_Model.md and the course offering build). The `/courses` catalog and program pages stay indexable too. While we're in the area, consider adding an `app/robots.ts` route that declares which paths are crawler-allowed vs disallowed (allow: /, /programs, /courses, /course/[slug], /teachers/[slug], /this-week; disallow: /account/*, /admin/*, /tools/*, /lessons/*, /session/*). Surfaced during the session-123 course offering schema discussion when Jesse asked whether lessons are protected from search engines.
notes: The real protection is the auth() redirect in lesson/session pages — Googlebot hits the URL with no session cookie, gets bounced to /login, never sees content to index. This is the standard practice for member-area routes. Noindex headers are insurance, not a fix. Also consider whether `/account/courses` (the member library) should be noindex'd; it's behind the auth gate already, so cosmetic. Don't noindex `/course/[slug]` itself — that page becomes a real public landing page after the offering build.

title: Session room: broadcast host change so all clients re-derive isSessionHost
description: After session 121 split the session-room permission into Session Host vs Co-host vs Participant, the End-for-All button and tile mute affordance are gated client-side on the value of `isSessionHost` that came back from the original token request. When the assigned host changes mid-session (Step in as Host upserts the HostAssignment to a new userId), the previous host's `isSessionHost` stays true client-side until they reload. They see End-for-All, click it, server returns 403, nothing happens. Server is authoritative so there's no security issue — it's a stale-UI problem. Fix: have step-in publish a 'host-changed' data-channel message with the new host's identity (topic: 'rim-session-role'). All clients listen via `room.on(RoomEvent.DataReceived)`, compare `localParticipant.identity === newHostIdentity`, update local `isSessionHost` state. Alternatively (cleaner): write `hostIdentity` into LiveKit room metadata via `RoomServiceClient.updateRoomMetadata` from step-in, have every client derive `isSessionHost` from `room.metadata.hostIdentity === localParticipant.identity`. Latecomers get the truth on connect; transitions get pushed via metadata-change events. Pairs naturally with backlog item 2026-05-24-002 (token route time-gate).
notes: Not a real-world problem in production — one assigned host per session, no rotation mid-session. Surfaces only in test scenarios where multiple host-team members deliberately click Step in as Host in sequence. Build only if a real session needs it or if we adopt a multi-host pattern.

title: Session room: server-side time gate on /api/livekit/token
description: The dashboard's Today card now correctly gates link visibility — regular members see Join only when start - 12min ≤ now ≤ end, hosts and teachers see Enter as Host from start - 22min. But the token route itself has no time gate. A regular member who knows the URL pattern `/session/<slug>` can navigate directly at any time and connect. Real-world risk is low (URL isn't surfaced anywhere else, sangha-scale community), but the dashboard is the only thing enforcing the time policy. Fix: in `/api/livekit/token`, compute today's occurrence's `liveStart` and `earlyOpenStart` (reuse the dashboard's date math by extracting into `lib/scheduleUtils.ts`), and gate token issuance: non-host/non-teacher → 403 before `liveStart`; host/teacher → 403 before `earlyOpenStart`. ADMIN bypass. Pair with backlog item 2026-05-24-001 if both are built — same token route, same `resolveSessionRole` helper.
notes: Closed 2026-05-26 (session 126). Implemented as a unified window helper `lib/sessionWindow.ts::getActiveSessionWindow` shared by both /api/livekit/token and /api/livekit/guest-token, with ADMIN/GUIDING_TEACHER bypass. Window opens 22 min before startDatetime and closes 30 min after endDatetime (+90 min fallback if endDatetime is null) — same shape for hosts and members rather than two epochs, since the per-session room model (also landed in this commit) makes the 22/12 split unnecessary. Defense-in-depth assertion `assertSessionDateInWindow` also wired into mute-participant, mute-all, end-session, and step-in so a client can't POST an arbitrary sessionDate. Commit 463f3bb.

title: PWA install — RIM as an installable app for Mac/PC/iOS/iPad/Android
description: Add a Progressive Web App manifest, icons, and service worker so users can install the RIM site as an app — File menu → 'Add to Dock' on Safari Mac (Sonoma+), 'Install' button in Chrome/Edge, 'Add to Home Screen' on iOS/iPad Safari and Android Chrome. The main operational win is permission persistence: installed PWAs get their own permission storage that's distinct from Safari's per-session sandbox, so the Greenroom flow auto-skips silently for installed-PWA users on every visit (Safari's per-session Allow no longer applies inside the PWA). Secondary wins: app icon on the home screen, standalone window without browser chrome, feels-like-an-app to non-technical users. Magic-code auth (shipped session 119) was the prerequisite — PWAs can't reliably receive magic-link clicks on iOS. Scope decision needed: install whole site as one PWA vs carve out just /session/* as a 'RIM Meeting' app. Whole-site is simpler and probably the right call; if /session/* is its own scope the install bar can appear contextually when a user visits a session room. Also needs a small in-app install prompt UI (banner or onboarding step) so users discover the install path — iOS's Add to Home Screen is buried in the share menu and most users won't find it without guidance.
notes: REJECTED in session 120 (2026-05-23) after explicit weighing against the RIM demographic (sangha 65+, tech-phobic, learned helplessness with new digital tools). iOS install ritual — open in Safari (not Chrome — Apple blocks Chrome from offering install), tap Share, scroll DOWN in the share sheet (option is below the fold on most iPhones), tap 'Add to Home Screen', tap 'Add' — is 4-5 steps in a menu most older users have never opened. Even with a platform-specific walkthrough page and annotated screenshots, the population we're designing for won't do it on their own; the realistic answer would be human help (asking a tech-comfortable family member), which is honest but not what 'installable app' is supposed to deliver. Native iOS/Android app was considered as the next-up alternative and also rejected (months of work, App Store gates, ongoing maintenance, and the initial install is itself a hurdle for the demographic). Moving sessions back to Zoom was considered as the third path and also rejected (would unwind the deliberate architectural decision in sessions 86/117/119 to transcend Zoom for this community via HostAssignment, ProgramTeacher, hub-as-authority, magic-code auth, deep integration). Final decision: the browser-based custom LiveKit room is the committed architecture. The Mac Safari permission friction is a known cost we accept; we invest in softening the in-browser flow (session 120's platform-aware Greenroom/Recovery instructions) and watch for real signal that more is needed. Next-best mitigations if needed later: phone dial-in via LiveKit SIP (audio-only fallback that preserves community presence — matches the 'tap a phone number' pattern this demographic actually uses), or a stronger Safari-Mac-specific pre-warning in the Greenroom. See session-log.md session 120 entry for the full architectural reasoning. Keeping this entry rather than deleting it so a future session that re-asks 'should we build a PWA?' can read the rejection and understand why before relitigating.

title: Rate-limit /api/auth/callback/resend to prevent code brute-force
description: After switching from magic link to 6-digit sign-in code (session 119), the verification callback at /api/auth/callback/resend accepts unlimited guesses. With a 900K keyspace (codes 100000–999999) and a 30-minute expiry window, a determined attacker who knows a victim's email could brute-force the code if request volume is unconstrained. Realistic risk at sangha scale is very low — attacker needs the email AND willingness to burn API requests against a small target — but worth adding rate limiting before any growth in user count or any expansion of who has accounts. Implementation options: (a) per-IP rate limit at the Vercel edge or in a Next.js middleware, (b) per-email rate limit stored in Redis/Neon with a sliding window, (c) NextAuth-side rate limit via a custom callback wrapper. Simplest is probably per-IP via Vercel's edge config or @upstash/ratelimit. Recommended threshold: 5 attempts per minute per IP across all auth endpoints.
notes: Closed 2026-05-27 (session 131). Shipped as a Postgres-backed fixed-window limiter on Neon — rejected Upstash/Redis as overkill for RIM's <100 sign-ins/day. New `rate_limit_windows` table + `lib/rateLimit.ts::checkRateLimit` atomic-UPSERT helper (single statement; three CASE branches for new-row / expired-reset / increment; RETURNING the post-write count — no read-modify-write race window). Wrapper at `app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` applies limits BOTH endpoints: signin/resend gets per-email (5/10min, defends email-bombing) + per-IP (20/10min, defends botnet hammering); callback/resend gets per-IP (20/10min, makes the 900K-code brute-force take ~350 days). Blocked → 303 redirect to `/login/error?error=RateLimit` with calm copy. Daily cleanup cron at 10:15 UTC. Migration `rate_limit_windows_v1`. Fails OPEN on DB error (User table is in same DB; DB-down already means nothing works). New per-area engineering doc `RIM_Auth.md` covers the architecture, thresholds, key namespacing convention, operational notes (clearing a stuck user, adjusting thresholds), and what-not-to-do. Commit 377d0f4.

title: Remove dead magic-link migration entries from prisma/migrate.mjs
description: Mechanical cleanup. After session 119 switched auth from magic link to magic code, the seed_magic_link_email_templates migration entry creates two rows that the next migration (seed_sign_in_code_email_templates) immediately deletes. Also the magic-link-* entries in organize_email_templates_with_groups_and_helptext reference now-deleted slugs. On fresh installs this is just wasted work, not a bug. Both can be safely removed from migrate.mjs (the migration flag system ensures the orgs are tied to specific flag names, so removing the entries from the JS array won't affect existing databases that already have the flags set). Low priority — no user impact.
notes: Touches prisma/migrate.mjs only. Remove the two old entries entirely (or comment them out for historical reference); do not touch the new sign-in-code entries. Verify with a fresh DB that the seed_sign_in_code_email_templates migration still produces both templates correctly without the prior magic-link entries existing.

title: Session room: Spotlight (host-driven global pin)
description: Zoom feature we don't have. Our local Speaker view auto-pins the active speaker locally; Spotlight pins one participant for everyone in the room, persists until the host releases it, and surfaces above the active-speaker logic. LiveKit doesn't have a built-in spotlight primitive, but we can implement it by sending a 'spotlight' data-channel message from the host and having every client treat the named identity as the auto-pin target until cleared. UI: a 'Spotlight for everyone' option in the per-tile host hover menu or in the participants panel's per-row host actions. Track current spotlight in room metadata so latecomers see it on join.
notes: Only build if a real session needs it. Most dharma talks don't — the active-speaker pin works fine. Could be useful for panel discussions or guided meditations where the teacher should stay focused regardless of who speaks.

title: Session room: Mirror video toggle in Settings
description: Zoom shows your self-view mirrored by default (matches the mirror you're used to looking in). We render the raw camera feed. Add a 'Mirror my video' toggle in the Video section of VideoSettingsPanel that applies a CSS scaleX(-1) transform only to the local participant's tile (not their video as published to others). Persist in localStorage under rim-livekit-prefs.
notes: Implementation: pass a 'mirror' boolean from VideoSettingsPanel down to RIMParticipantTile. Tile compares trackRef.participant.identity to room.localParticipant.identity and applies '.rim-tile-wrapper--mirror' class only when match. CSS: .rim-tile-wrapper--mirror .lk-participant-video { transform: scaleX(-1); }.

title: Session room: Test Microphone + Test Speakers in Settings
description: Useful pre-session affordance. Test Microphone: 5-second VU-meter showing input volume. Test Speakers: plays a short bell or chime through the selected output device so user can confirm they'll hear the session. Both live in the Audio section of VideoSettingsPanel below the device dropdowns.
notes: Use getUserMedia({ audio: { deviceId: selectedMicId } }) for the test mic; pipe MediaStreamSource through AnalyserNode for VU. Test speakers: a short asset bundled in /public/sounds/, played via Audio element with .setSinkId(selectedSpeakerId) to honor the chosen output.

title: Session room: harden host tag against client spoofing
description: Currently host: true is seeded into participant metadata at token-issue time. The token grants canUpdateOwnMetadata: true so a client can technically rewrite their own metadata in devtools to claim Host. Real host actions (mute, end-for-all) are server-gated via auth() + role + HostAssignment + ProgramTeacher lookup, so this is a UI-only deception risk. To eliminate: route avatar and signal metadata updates through a small server endpoint that calls RoomServiceClient.updateParticipant (server is the only writer), and drop canUpdateOwnMetadata from the token grant. Pattern: POST /api/livekit/metadata with the requested partial; server validates ownership and applies.
notes: Risk-accepted in session 117 for a small trusted Sangha. Worth doing if (a) the community grows large enough that trust no longer covers it, or (b) we ever expose the room beyond authenticated members + key-gated guests. Documented in app/api/livekit/token/route.ts.

title: Session room: chevron 'Audio Settings…' link scrolls to section
description: DevicePickerMenu's bottom links — 'Audio Settings…' and 'Camera Settings…' — open VideoSettingsPanel but don't scroll the panel to the relevant section. Sections are short and the panel body is single-page-scrollable, so this is a minor friction. Accept an optional focusSection: 'audio' | 'video' | 'presence' prop on VideoSettingsPanel; on mount, scrollIntoView the matching section's element.

title: Decide on functional Vercel preview deploys (staging DB or build-only)
description: Session 116 surfaced that Vercel preview builds for non-main branches were failing because prisma/migrate.mjs needs POSTGRES_PRISMA_URL and Vercel preview envs don't inherit production env vars by default. Added a guard at the top of migrate.mjs main() so it skips cleanly when the env is missing — production deploys are unaffected, and preview builds now reach next build without crashing. BUT: the app itself still has no DB at runtime on preview deploys, so any page that hits Prisma will 500 if visited. Two options for the future: (A) provision a small staging/preview Postgres (Neon supports branching — could use a Neon branch as the preview DB, scoped to Vercel's Preview env) and wire its URL to the Preview env scope so previews are functional end-to-end; or (B) accept that previews are build-only checks and not visit-them deployments — in which case maybe configure Vercel to skip preview deploys for most pushes, or just leave the situation as-is. Decision-point: do we want previews to be functional? If yes, set up the branched Neon DB and add it to Vercel Preview env. If no, document the limitation and move on.
notes: Branch pushes are rare in current workflow — Jesse usually goes straight to main. But the moment a branch-based workflow comes back (a real PR, a Claude worktree pass that wants to be reviewed visually before merging), this matters. Not urgent until then. Neon branching is the cleanest path if we go (A) — see https://neon.tech/docs/guides/vercel-overview for the Vercel integration that auto-creates a branch DB per preview deploy.

title: Drop legacy HubConversationThread.status column
description: Session 115 added archivedAt/archivedById to hub_conversation_threads and unified the archive mechanism with HubDocument. The legacy status column (OPEN | CLOSED) is now vestigial: the PATCH handler keeps it in sync with archivedAt for backward compat. Once a few UI reads are migrated to use archivedAt directly, the status column can be dropped. Sites to migrate: components/HubConvThreadClient.tsx:195 (const isClosed = thread.status !== 'OPEN'), components/HubConvClient.tsx:349/440/443/452 (status display + archive toggle buttons), the document conversations POST that initializes status: 'OPEN' on create, and the hub conversations POST that does the same (both can stop writing the field once it's dropped). Then add a migration that drops the column and the @default('OPEN'). Mechanical, low-risk, no rush — purely a model-cleanup item.
notes: Wait until at least one full release cycle passes after session 115 so the in-sync writes have backfilled any rows touched. Then audit grep for remaining 'thread.status' / 'status: "OPEN"' / 'status: "CLOSED"' references.

title: Coordinator-friendly hub content editing for non-host hubs
description: Hub welcomeBody and homeContent are editable inline on the host hub (HostHubHomeClient has an inline edit affordance for coordinators). For the other three hubs (courses, registrar, support), there's no inline editor — coordinators can only edit hub content via /admin/hubs/[slug]/edit, which is strictly ADMIN-only. Session 115 surfaced this when the sidebar Settings link was gated to ADMIN only (matching actual page authorization) — coordinators have no path to edit their hub's welcome message. Two design options: (A) extend HostHubHomeClient's inline edit affordance to all hubs (drop the host-team specific 'Our offerings this month' panel into a hasSchedule branch, keep the welcome editor generic); or (B) build a separate coordinator-scoped /account/hub/[slug]/settings page with welcomeHeadline + welcomeBody + homeContent + conversationCategories editors. Option A is less new UI, keeps editing close to the surface it affects; option B is a cleaner separation between view and edit. Either way, the coordinator-vs-admin distinction needs to be carried through — coordinators edit content fields, admins edit config fields (slug, type, app links, hard-remove coordinators).
notes: Lower urgency than the broader Webflow migration. Currently the only impacted users are coordinators of courses/registrar/support hubs, and those teams aren't yet active. Worth handling before each non-host hub is staffed — but the session 115 welcome seeds buy time.

title: Phase 2: Authenticated CTA states on Webflow Program Detail
description: Extend the ctaHtml pattern on /api/public/programs/[slug] to cover the four authenticated states the RIM Next public detail page already renders: (1) registered — '✓ You’re registered. View your program details'; (2) waitlisted — 'You’re on the waitlist. View details'; (3) open virtual program + logged-in — 'Access Zoom Link in Dashboard →'; (4) open in-person/hybrid + logged-in — 'Simply arrive in person · Zoom link in dashboard'. Requires an authenticated endpoint — /api/member/programs/[slug]/cta-state — that returns either a session: null response (no override) or an ctaHtmlOverride string. rim-connect.js extends to optionally fetch the authenticated endpoint alongside the public one; if it returns an override, it replaces ctaHtml before populating. No Webflow change needed — the existing single-placeholder pattern carries through. Key architectural decision: the auth bridge between Webflow (www.rootedinmindfulness.org) and RIM Next API (rim-next.vercel.app). Three options: (A) move RIM Next API behind api.rootedinmindfulness.org subdomain and set the NextAuth session cookie on .rootedinmindfulness.org so it is sent cross-subdomain; (B) token-based: member logs in via a Webflow-hosted form that calls /api/auth/signin-token, stores a short-lived JWT in localStorage, sends it as Authorization: Bearer on each member API call; (C) iframe + postMessage hand-shake. Option A is the cleanest production model and unblocks the broader member-area migration (dashboard, my-programs, registration, settings) — do this one right once and every future member feature on Webflow rides on it. Option B is a faster bootstrap if subdomain change is blocked. Include CORS + credentials:true configuration on all /api/member/* routes and an allowlist of Webflow origins. Test matrix: four guest states (current), four member states, logout transitions, deadline crossing (registrationClosed flipping mid-session).
notes: Builds on the single-placeholder CTA pattern established in session 92 (ctaHtml on /api/public/programs/[slug], one placeholder Block in Webflow). The auth-bridge decision is load-bearing for every Webflow member feature — draft and confirm with Jesse before implementing. Good candidate for a dedicated design session rather than ad-hoc work.

title: Dedup Aside blocks in migrated program descriptions
description: The session-91 fold_special_notes_into_description_as_aside migration prepended an Aside to each program's description, but at least one program (Awakening The Heart) already contained a manually-added Aside from session-90 testing — producing two identical Aside boxes on the public page. Need a one-time dedup migration that walks each program's description, detects consecutive or identical Aside blocks (by comparing normalized child content), and removes the duplicates. Low risk: only acts on programs with the duplication pattern. Also worth adding as a forward-guard in future field-sunset migrations: scan the destination field for an existing matching block before prepending, so this pattern can't recur for Announcement / EarlyArrival / DanaInvitation / etc.
notes: Interim fix available: authors can manually delete the duplicate Aside in the Program Editor's Content tab. Dedup migration only needed if the duplication turns out to affect several programs.

Replaces the current pattern where the dashboard links to the public marketing page. Should include: registration status, Zoom/join link, calendar links (Google/Apple), pending actions (complete dana, update info), program logistics (next session date/time, location). Priority: Donate, Volunteer, Community Membership, Login. Lower priority: Diversity, Kalyana Mitta, Glossary, Magazine Articles.

title: Admin File Manager — /admin/files
description: Build an admin page that shows every file uploaded via editors (Vercel Blob), grouped by where it lives in the app: hub documents, lessons, program descriptions, course descriptions, etc. Should display: total count and storage size, per-file location (which document / hub / program references it), size, upload date, and a clear 'orphans' section — blobs that exist in storage but are not referenced by any DB row. Each orphan gets a Delete button; bulk-delete-orphans for the common case. Also: wrap all content-bearing update/delete API routes in a shared `withContentCleanup()` helper so blob cleanup can't be forgotten when new editor surfaces are added.
notes: Currently cleanupRemovedBlobs/cleanupAllBlobs is wired only in hub/[slug]/documents and lessons routes. Program descriptions, manual sections, hub announcements, support replies do not clean up attachments on delete, so those can leak. The page would make leaks visible instantly and expose storage cost. Optional follow-up: a weekly cron that auto-sweeps orphans older than 24h.

title: Rich Callouts — container blocks with preset variants
description: Rebuild the callout as a container block (BlockNote spec with children) so the body supports lists, numbered steps, and nested paragraphs — not just inline marks. Keep variants as a curated preset list (no user-picked icons) so each variant carries a consistent meaning.
notes: Built in session 87 — but not as a single six-variant Callout. Split into five distinct editorial elements: Pull Quote, Verse Quote, Practice Suggestion (container), Reflection (container), and Note/Decision Callout (container). Rationale: each role deserves its own visual vocabulary, not a shared box with different accent colors. Container-body pattern (content: none + children) and defensive migration seeding are in place for all three container blocks.

title: Migrate Program specialNotes into SpecialNote block

Once that block exists, this migration becomes the template for Program.specialAnnouncement, Program.earlyArrivalMessage, Program.pullQuote pair, on-page Program.danaMessage, Lesson.headerQuote pair, and Lesson.reflectionPrompt.

title: Add shortName field to Program model
description: The Host Schedule calendar shows up to three program-name pills per day cell at ~12px font in ~110px-wide cells. Names longer than ~18 characters truncate with an ellipsis (e.g. 'Private Teacher Meetings' becomes 'Private Teach…'). Add an optional `shortName` field to the Program model so admins can set a readable abbreviation ('Private Teacher', 'Silent Meditation', 'Awakening'). The calendar pill display would use `shortName || name` with existing truncation as a fallback.
notes: Raised during session 88 Host Schedule redesign. Fields to update: Prisma Program model (new optional String), prisma/migrate.mjs (new idempotent migration), Program Editor Content tab (new input), `pillLabel()` function in `components/HubScheduleClient.tsx` (prefer shortName when present). No schema dependency since field is optional.

title: Architectural question: Step In gate vs. automatic host capability for all host-team members
description: Current model: host-team members who are not the assigned host must explicitly click 'Step in as Host' to gain host controls in the LiveKit session room. Simpler model: any active host-team HubMember automatically receives host token grants, removing the Step In gate entirely. The role design's two-host ideal — one host on the relational side, one on the technical — arguably fits the simpler model better: both should have controls from the moment they join. Tradeoffs: simpler model reduces friction and better matches a small trusted team; explicit Step In preserves responsibility clarity (one named host, others are guests who can upgrade). Decision should be made post-cutover unless training surfaces friction with the current model first.
notes: Surfaced during T2 (session room chapter, session 105). The Step In button is wired in app/session/[slug]/page.tsx — isHostTeam && !isHost conditional renders it. Token grant logic is in app/api/livekit/token/route.ts. If the simpler model is chosen, the Step In button and /api/livekit/step-in route can be removed.

title: Mobile audit for remaining hub tools and pages
description: Session 88 discovered that app/layout.tsx was missing a viewport meta tag — every route on the site had been rendering at ~980px desktop width on mobile and ignoring every @media (max-width: 768px) rule in custom.css. Viewport meta is now in place, which means existing mobile styles finally fire. Host Schedule got a focused mobile-friendliness pass (44px touch targets, iOS 16px input fix, chrome compression, two-tap confirm). Other hub tools and internal hub pages need the same treatment: /tools/programs, /tools/learning, /account/hub/[slug]/conversations, /account/hub/[slug]/documents, /account/hub/[slug]/members, /account/hub/[slug]/trash. Public pages (homepage, /community-programs, /this-week, /teachers, /courses, /programs/[slug], /lessons/[slug]) should also be re-tested — they weren't using their mobile styles either.
notes: Pattern to apply per tool: 44px touch targets on buttons/links, 16px font on text inputs (.fi/.ft/.fs already fixed globally at <768px), chrome compression for short viewports, defensive max-width on cards. Use the hub-schedule CSS block (~11915 in custom.css) as a reference pattern.

title: Guiding Teacher presence badge in hubs

The legibility half of the 'can walk into any room but is seen when they do' principle. The role doc deferred this badge originally; the session-135 access change is what makes it earn its place. Matters most the day RIM has a second guiding teacher. Compute per-viewer where coordinator status is already derived (effectiveCoordinator); surface in HubWorkspaceSidebar / member roster / participant tile as appropriate.
